name: Sarah K. Campbell
description: Concurred, argued that the trial court lacked jurisdiction to realign sentences because no statute authorized such modification of a final criminal judgment, thereby upholding the principle of finality.

name: HOLLY KIRBY
description: Dissented, argued that Ms. Hunt has standing to challenge her unconstitutionally misnumbered voting district because she suffered representational harm, which is an actual and imminent injury, and the majority's analysis on standing is flawed.

name: ROGER A. PAGE
description: Concurred, argued that a positive alert from a drug-sniffing canine, combined with other suspicious facts, establishes probable cause for a vehicle search, even with the legalization of hemp.

name: ROBERT L. HOLLOWAY, JR.
description: Concurred, argued that Public Chapter 182 is constitutional as the duties of the district attorney are largely defined by statute, and collateral review proceedings are quasi-civil, not criminal prosecutions, thus not infringing Article VI, § 5.

name: HOLLY KIRBY
description: Concurred, argued that the right to petition in the Tennessee Constitution applies only to governmental entities, not private parties, and cannot be a basis for retaliatory discharge against private employers.

name: SARAH K. CAMPBELL
description: Concurred, and filed a separate concurring opinion.

name: JEFFREY USMAN
description: Concurred, argued that the statute is facially constitutional but unconstitutional as applied to the plaintiffs, and affirmed the award of nominal damages.

name: Sharon G. Lee
description: Concurred, argued that Rule 13 provisions are constitutional as applied, the Petitioner was not unconstitutionally denied appellate review, and he received a full and fair post-conviction hearing.

name: Jeffrey S. Bivins
description: Concurred, argued that to regain suffrage rights in Tennessee, individuals convicted of infamous crimes in other states must comply with both sections 2-19-143(3) and 40-29-202.

name: Sharon G. Lee
description: Dissented, argued that Mr. Falls' voting rights were fully restored by Virginia's clemency under section 2-19-143(3) and he should not be subjected to additional re-enfranchisement requirements of section 40-29-202, as the right to vote is fundamental.

name: Roger A. Page, Chief Justice
description: Concurred, argued that the ESA Act only regulates Local Education Agencies (LEAs), which are distinct from county governments, and therefore does not implicate the Home Rule Amendment.

name: Thomas R. Frierson, II, Sp. J.
Sharon G. Lee, J.
description: Dissented, argued that the ESA Act substantially affects the Plaintiffs' local control and sovereignty, thereby implicating the Home Rule Amendment and rendering the Act unconstitutional without local approval.

name: Holly Kirby, J.
description: Dissented with Sharon G. Lee, J.'s opinion.
